recipe.name: P4 Walk-around
recipe.hook_formula: Point at the equipment: what the driver will actually drive, then the strongest fact.
recipe.image_prompt_template: Our tractor parked in a {setting}, three-quarter view, no text, no logos, no lettering
recipe.motion_template: A slow orbit around the tractor

en.primary_text: Regional tanker runs through Illinois, Indiana, and Wisconsin. You earn $0.75 per mile, get paid weekly, and are home weekends. Pet policy available. Class A, tanker and hazmat endorsements required. Age 23+, 2 years experience required.
en.headline: Home weekends. Weekly pay.

es.headline: Casa fines de semana. Pago semanal.

es.headline: Se buscan choferes clase A

en.headline: Great pay, great team

es.primary_text: Emocionante oportunidad para conductores Clase A de unirse a nuestro equipo dinámico. Ofrecemos pago competitivo, excelente carga y un ambiente familiar donde valoramos a nuestros conductores. Gana $0.75 por milla. A

scores.reason: The hook ignores the concept entirely — it leads with vague praise, not equipment or rate. Primary_text is packed with filler ('exciting opportunity,' 'dynamic team,' 'competitive pay,' 'family atmosphere,' 'truly value our drivers'). Region, endorsements, age, and experience requirements are all missing. Spanish is a word-for-word translation with no trade voice.

Hook nails the concept: equipment first, strongest fact second. Primary_text covers region (IL/IN/WI), pay, weekly pay, home weekends, pet policy, endorsements, age, and experience — every fact is present. Plain, dispatcher-style sentences. Spanish uses 'tráiler,' 'rutas,' 'endoso,' distances in miles, and reads naturally; headline is correctly adapted rather than translated literally.

Hook matches the concept well. Primary_text states the rate and CDL/experience requirements, but drops the region (IL/IN/WI), home weekends, weekly pay, pet policy, hazmat/tanker endorsements, and age minimum — most facts are missing. 'Let's talk' and 'if you have the miles behind you' are mild filler. Spanish omits the same facts and 'únete al equipo' is soft filler.
